articles.headline: The oldest grudge in football
articles.description: When Texas Tech and its brash benefactor bought their way into the college football big time, they were settling an old West Texas score.

images.name: Texas Tech [1296x729]
images.caption: Behind the vision and backing of billionaire donor Cody Campbell, coach Joey McGuire and the Red Raiders have embraced a role of disruptors as college football's villians and are trying to become a new power.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 1 [946x947]
images.caption: The Santa Rita No. 1 ushered in a new era of oil exploration in the Permian Basin.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 2 [2929x2000]
images.alt: The oil that won World War II.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 3 [2693x1616]
images.caption: Preston Smith (right) was the first Texas governor from West Texas. He was a student at Texas Technological College.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 4 [2933x1339]
images.caption: The original Four Sixes barn from 1908 is now on the Texas Tech campus at the National Ranching Heritage Center.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 5 [2000x3000]
images.caption: Four relief carvings on the facade of a building at Texas Tech.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 6 [1987x1365]
images.caption: Cody Campbell, a fourth-generation Red Raider, and his son, Carson, a 2029 recruit, talking to Pat McAfee on the "College GameDay" set.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 7 [2999x1940]
images.caption: Vintage oil and gas signs at Cooks Garage in Lubbock.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 8 [2999x1999]
images.caption: Lugene Pickering, the 1975 Texas Tech homecoming queen, has been a devoted Red Raiders fan since birth and makes a homemade cobbler for coach Joey McGuire and takes it to his house to show her appreciation after each Tech win.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 11 [2836x1860]
images.caption: Texas Tech's Masked Rider, Sofie Jones, leads the charge onto the field before every Red Raiders game, a proud tradition. Left, trophies commemorate Texas Tech players who have won Super Bowls.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 12 [2625x1333]
images.caption: There isn't much cover from the wide-open skies in West Texas, but red-and-black-clad fans are accustomed to handling an unpredictable environment.

images.name: Texas Tech - Inline 13 [1601x1020]
images.caption: Taylor Sheridan, part of a group that owns the legendary Four Sixes Ranch, has long admired Texas Tech football. Right, Eclipse Windmills were used across the West Texas to drill for water on ranches and hauled onto job sites like building railroads.

images.name: Texas Tech - 36x [1785x1494]
images.caption: Texas Tech owes a lot, past and present, to the oilfield, and proudly displays its pride, including T-shirts that say "Thank you for filling up your gas tank" with the Red Raiders' Double-T logo on them.
images.alt: An old oil rig painted in Texas Tech colors.

article.headline: Cardell Williams throws for a TD with 2:11 left and Maryland adds late FG to beat Wisconsin 24-21
article.description: — Backup quarterback Cardell Williams ran for two touchdowns and threw for the tying score with 2:11 remining as Maryland beat Wisconsin 24-21 on Saturday to secure back-to-back conference victories for the first time since 2023.
article.linkText: Cardell Williams throws for a TD with 2:11 left and Maryland adds late FG to beat Wisconsin 24-21
article.story: COLLEGE PARK, Md. -- — Backup quarterback Cardell Williams ran for two touchdowns and threw for the tying score with 2:11 remining as Maryland beat Wisconsin 24-21 on Saturday to secure back-to-back conference victories for the first time since 2023. It was a 32-game span between consecutive conference victories for Maryland (4-6, 2-5 Big Ten), which beat Michigan State and Indiana in September of 2023. Maryland trailed 21-14 early in the fourth quarter before holding the Badgers to a three-and-out on their next two drives. Then, Williams found Preston Howard wide open down the right sideline and he went untouched for a 39-yard score to tie it with just over two minutes left. Williams' first touchdown pass as a Terp was his 19th consecutive completion — to break Malik Washington's program record of 18 set on Sept. 12, 2026, at UConn. Maryland linebacker Trey Reddick had a blindside hit on Wisconsin freshman quarterback Ryan Hopkins and the ball came out, recovered by Eyan Thomas at the Badgers' 33-yard line with 1:52 left. Five straight rushes by Williams set up Sean O’Haire for the winning 30-yard field goal with 29 seconds left. “They believe that as long as there are seconds on the clock, somebody can make a play,” interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim said. Williams was 21 of 23 for 183 yards and carried it 11 times for 17 yards and two short scores. Williams, a transfer from Sacramento State, made his first start in place of the injured Washington, who was wearing a left knee brace after a game-time decision. “I’m happy for Cardell in that he got the opportunity to play in a Power 4 football game," Abdul-Rahim said. "It’s also a testament to how we prepare as a staff and infuse confidence into the next man up. I’m really happy that he was able to excel.” Hopkins, who earned the Big Ten freshman of the week honors after throwing for three touchdowns in his starting debut last week, was 11 of 22 for 77 yards for Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3). The Badgers were just 2 of 13 on third downs. Mason Posa had a game-high 13 tackles to reach double digits for the fourth straight game. Maryland's defense forced three turnovers and limited the Badgers to 201 total yards. The Terps are the only team in the Big Ten that has forced a turnover in every conference game this season. The Badgers’ only other loss in this six-game series came last season when the Terrapins earned a 27-10 victory in Madison. Up next Wisconsin plays at Purdue next Saturday.
